previous_statement: The open scope challenge is decisive, not a bridgeable proof gap: under the registered all-real-A contract, P=I_2, a=e_1, b=e_2, chi(x)=x_1, N=empty, A=-1, and Lambda=1 satisfy every hypothesis but give left side 2 and right side 3. The ledger sandwich uses A*sum_N|d_Q| <= A*l_chi and is valid only for A>=0. Therefore node 1.3 cannot prove the registered theorem; the registry contract and AF root must first be repaired identically by adding A>=0.
new_statement: Under the current root hypothesis A>0, node 1.2 gives (1-A*l_chi)/Lambda <= sum_{Q in F}|d_Q|. Applying lem-hx-signed-variation-ledger to the ordered pair (a,b) and the fiber set S=F gives sum_{Q in F}|d_Q| <= a^+(F)+b^+(F)+nu(a)+nu(b), with exactly the same d_Q=sum_{j in Q}(a_j-b_j). Chaining these inequalities and subtracting nu(a)+nu(b) from both sides yields a^+(F)+b^+(F) >= (1-A*l_chi)/Lambda-nu(a)-nu(b), which is the conclusion of node 1.
